findings.title: Delete query's retryCount condition is not scoped to SMS reminders
Retry threshold is inconsistent and drops reminders after only two attempts
The retry-count update inside the catch block can throw and abort the whole loop
Duplicated retry-increment logic that uses read-then-write instead of an atomic increment

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Delete query's retryCount condition is not scoped to SMS reminders

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43

Explanation:
The `OR` makes the second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` match reminders of every method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, and so on). The SMS cron job could therefore delete non-SMS reminders. At the moment only the SMS handler increments `retryCount`, but other handlers or later changes could set it, and the delete would then remove their rows. Scope the retry branch to `method: SMS`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
OR: [
  { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } },
  { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } },
],
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Retry threshold is inconsistent and drops reminders after only two attempts

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39-41

Explanation:
`gt: 1` deletes a reminder once `retryCount` reaches 2, so a reminder gets only two failed attempts before it is removed. The delete runs at the start of each cron run, so the count is checked before the next attempt. Define a named constant for the maximum retries and use `gte` against it, so the intent is clear and easy to change.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const MAX_RETRIES = 3;
// ...
retryCount: { gte: MAX_RETRIES }
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: The retry-count update inside the catch block can throw and abort the whole loop

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190-197

Explanation:
`prisma.workflowReminder.update` runs inside `catch` without its own try/catch. If the DB call fails, for example because the row was already deleted or the connection dropped, the exception escapes the loop. The remaining reminders are then not processed and the handler returns a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which does not throw on a missing row.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
} catch (error) {
  console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`);
  try {
    await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } });
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`Failed to update retryCount: ${e}`);
  }
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Duplicated retry-increment logic that uses read-then-write instead of an atomic increment

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-197

Explanation:
The same update appears twice, and both copies compute `reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier. Overlapping cron runs could overwrite each other's counts. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` and move the update into a helper.
